skill.description: Fetch current Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama model identifiers. Classify models into fast, default, or heavy tiers and detect new entries.

skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: No malicious intent or prompt injection was found, and most alerts are documentation or language-token false positives. Confirmed risks include broad parent .env loading, credentials in curl arguments or URLs, an unvalidated Ollama host, and a predictable temporary path.

remediation.suggestion: Remove parent-directory searches. Require explicit environment injection or an explicit .env path limited to the current project.

remediation.issue: Credentials exposed in command arguments and URLs
remediation.suggestion: Use provider SDKs or a native HTTP client. Keep credentials out of command arguments, query strings, logs, and diagnostics.
Validate the URL scheme and hostname. Default to loopback addresses and require explicit approval before contacting remote hosts.
Use mktemp with restrictive permissions, or process the command output directly without creating a shared temporary file.

content.user_title: Discover Current AI Models and Tiers
content.value_statement: Model identifiers change and quickly make configurations stale. This skill queries supported providers, caches results, detects additions, and recommends capability tiers.
actual_capabilities: Fetches model lists from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and Ollama endpoints.
Caches provider responses and reuses fresh results for up to 24 hours.
Detects model identifiers that are absent from the known-model registry.
Infers fast, default, or heavy tiers from configurable naming patterns.
Supports JSON reporting, automatic classification, interactive classification, and dry runs.
limitations: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini queries require valid provider API credentials.
OpenAI discovery currently filters results to model identifiers beginning with gpt-5.2.
Tier inference depends on naming patterns and can misclassify unfamiliar model families.
Ollama discovery only lists models available at the configured host.

use_cases.title: Refresh application model identifiers
use_cases.description: Check provider APIs before updating production model configuration or deployment settings.

use_cases.title: Choose a task-appropriate model tier
use_cases.description: Compare fast, default, and heavy recommendations for latency, cost, and capability needs.

use_cases.title: Monitor newly available models
use_cases.description: Detect unclassified provider models and review suggested tiers before adding them to the registry.

prompt_templates.title: List cached models
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the cached models for each provider. Include the fetch timestamp and any provider errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with existing data and avoid network requests.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh one provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh models for [provider]. Summarize available identifiers and note any authentication or connection errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve current identifiers from one provider.

prompt_templates.title: Recommend model tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Review current models for [provider]. Recommend fast, default, and heavy options with concise reasons based on available metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and classify new models
prompt_templates.prompt: Refresh all enabled providers, detect unknown models, and propose tiers. Do not update the registry until I approve each uncertain classification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Perform a controlled catalog update across providers.

output_examples.input: Show current Anthropic model tiers from the local configuration.
Check whether any fetched OpenAI models need classification.
output_examples.output: Two new OpenAI models were detected. One matches the fast pattern, while one needs manual classification.

output_examples.input: Explain why Ollama discovery returned no models.
output_examples.output: The configured Ollama host returned an empty model list. Confirm the service is running and that models have been pulled.

best_practices: Review cached timestamps before making network requests.
Inspect provider errors before using returned model identifiers.
Approve uncertain tier assignments manually before updating the known-model registry.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode provider model versions without checking current availability.
Do not place API credentials in prompts, logs, or shared output.
Do not auto-classify unfamiliar models when no naming pattern matches.

faq.question: Which providers are supported?
faq.answer: The skill supports Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, and Ollama.

faq.question: Which credentials are required?
faq.answer: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini require their documented API keys. Ollama requires no key by default.

faq.question: Does the skill cache provider responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It stores model results locally and treats them as fresh for 24 hours.

faq.question: How are models assigned to tiers?
faq.answer: Configurable name patterns infer fast, default, or heavy tiers. Unmatched models can be reviewed interactively.

faq.question: Can it update classifications automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. Automatic mode saves inferred tiers, while dry-run mode reports changes without writing them.

faq.question: Does it verify model quality or pricing?
faq.answer: No. It discovers model metadata and applies naming rules. It does not benchmark quality, latency, pricing, or availability guarantees.
